content: 1. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. When co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, monitor the levels of these substrates closely. If necessary, consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate to maintain therapeutic efficacy. 2. Elagolix decreases the plasma levels of methadone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring of methadone levels is recommended, and therapy adjustments may be required. 3. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of methotrexate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 4. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of methsuximide by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. As elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, sensitive CYP2C19 substrates should be used with caution, and therapy should be closely monitored. 5. Elagolix decreases the levels of methylergonovine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 6. Elagolix decreases the levels of methylprednisolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider dose adjustments and monitor closely. 7. Elagolix decreases the levels of midazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. For oral midazolam, consider increasing the dose if needed, and monitor closely. 8. Elagolix decreases the levels of midostaurin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Additionally, mifepristone increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 10. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended due to the risk of significant drug interactions. 11. Elagolix decreases the levels of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 12. Elagolix decreases the levels of mirtazapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of mitomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered due to the potential for significant interaction. 15. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during concomitant use, and additional barrier methods should be considered. 16. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Conversely, elagolix decreases the levels of modafinil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. 17. Elagolix decreases the levels of montelukast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 18. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of morphine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of nadolol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of naldemedine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it also decreases naldemedine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Elagolix decreases the levels of naloxegol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 23. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 24. Elagolix decreases the levels of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 25. Elagolix decreases the levels of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Elagolix decreases the levels of nevirapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 27. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases nicardipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Elagolix decreases the levels of nifedipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 29. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases nilotinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Elagolix decreases the levels of nimodipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 31. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Elagolix decreases the levels of nisoldipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 33. Elagolix decreases the levels of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Elagolix decreases the levels of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 35. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Moderate CYP3A4 inducers may decrease progestin concentrations; additional barrier methods should be considered. 36. Elagolix decreases the levels of olaparib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 37. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of olutasidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decrease olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. Alternative therapies should be considered. 38. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 39. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir increase the levels or effects of elagolix through mechanisms involving OATP1B1/1B3 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. No dose adjustments are needed for omeprazole at 40 mg/day or less. However, elagolix decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases ondansetron levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 42. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases osimertinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 43. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. However, it decreases ospemifene levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 44. Elagolix decreases the levels of oxycodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases paclitaxel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 46. Elagolix decreases the levels of palbociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely.
